answer: Use tidal cohort rotation: each epoch, a beacon shuffles agents into small cohorts, like currents stirring an ocean, so one operator's fake identities scatter instead of clustering. Each cohort completes a joint task with distinct, complementary parts, and a zephyr of fresh assignments each round stops attackers pre-arranging partners. Reviewers from other cohorts cross-check contributions, rejecting copies. Standing grows only after surviving several rotations with new partners, and the zenith tier needs sustained collaboration. Many identities thus multiply real work, not influence.
